Daily Digest Monday, September 7, 2026

"The Marketing Stack Is Dead," 96% Use AI But Hiring Shifts to Judgment, 6sense Routes Intent to AI Agents

Totaligent declares martech dead. B2B marketers hit 96% AI adoption but face talent gap. 6sense feeds intent data to Claude and ChatGPT.

  1. 1

    Totaligent: "The Marketing Stack Is Dead. AI Wrote the Obituary."

    A new white paper delivers the harshest verdict yet on martech sprawl: 15,500+ products, utilization near 50%, and martech's share of marketing budgets at a multi-year low — even as paid media spend rose. The argument: enterprise marketing is resetting from a "rented stack of disconnected tools" to a unified communications operating system. PMMs who tied positioning to point solutions may need to rethink.

    Read on GlobeNewswire ↗
  2. 2

    96% of B2B Marketers Use AI, But Hiring Is Shifting to Judgment Roles

    Three separate 2026 research releases converge on the same reality: the AI tool rollout is largely done; the hard part is now governance, data plumbing, and talent design. HubSpot finds 80% of marketers use AI to create content, while Demand Gen Report puts adoption at 96%. But the hiring shift is toward QA, judgment, and orchestration — not more prompt engineers. The efficiency lever (45% cite it as top benefit) is real, but so is the skills gap.

    Read on MarketScale ↗
  3. 3

    6sense Routes B2B Intent Data Directly to AI Agents

    6sense launched product updates that pipe revenue data — B2B intent signals, account stages, buying predictions — directly into external AI agents like Claude, ChatGPT, and Agentforce. This is the "agents reading your CRM" vision going live: AI systems now consume intent data natively, not through dashboards. For PMMs, it means positioning and battlecards may need to be AI-readable, not just human-readable.

    Read on MarTech ↗
  4. 4

    Sitefire (YC W26): Marketing to AI Agents, Not Humans

    Y Combinator's Winter '26 batch includes Sitefire, a startup that helps brands market their products to AI agents. The thesis: as ChatGPT, Claude, and OpenClaw become discovery surfaces, brands need content and structured data that AI agents can parse. Sitefire identifies which content drives AI visibility and auto-generates it. It's the first real "AI SEO" play — and a sign that product marketing may soon have two audiences.

    View on YC ↗
  5. 5

    Meta's AI Agent "Hatch" Launches Inside WhatsApp and Instagram

    Following its $18B settlement, Meta is reportedly releasing Hatch, a consumer AI agent that runs inside WhatsApp and Instagram. The agent can perform autonomous tasks including online purchases and restaurant bookings. For enterprise marketers, this is the B2C version of what 6sense is doing for B2B: AI agents making decisions on behalf of users. The implication for PMM: your messaging may need to convince an agent before it convinces a human. Read this one: The MarketScale piece on AI adoption vs. data/talent readiness. The stat that jumps out: 96% adoption, but the hiring shift is toward judgment roles — QA, orchestration, governance. This is the real 2026 story. Tool rollout is done. The moat is now human oversight of AI systems, not more AI tools. PMMs who can audit, validate, and govern AI outputs will have leverage.

    Read on CNBC ↗
